src/models/ChatGoogleAI.ts:1.why: ChatGoogleAI extends langchain ChatOpenAI and is constructed in src/models/index.ts:133 for the gemini provider branch, with openAIApiKey set to providerInfo.apiKey, the end users own Google AI Studio key stored in their browser, same BYOK architecture and same operator key gap as the other provider branches in this factory.

src/models/CustomChatAnthropic.ts:211.why: Client-side browser extension, no backend. apiKey comes only from inputs.apiKey, sourced in src/models/index.ts:175 from providerInfo.apiKey, the end user own key typed into Settings and stored in this browser Dexie/chrome.storage. The globalThis.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fallback at line 225 is dead code, nothing ever sets that global. Router needs one operator-held RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY per deployment; this app has no operator key and no secure place to hold one, since any secret baked into the extension bundle is extractable by every installer who could then bill the operators Router account. Moving this BYOK traffic through a shared Router key would swap each users own provider credentials and billing for the developers, which breaks the products BYOK promise.

src/models/CustomChatOpenAI.ts:214.why: Same BYOK architecture as the Anthropic site: this client is constructed in src/models/index.ts, in every branch openAIApiKey and baseURL come from providerInfo loaded via getOpenAIConfigById, the end users own stored key and chosen endpoint, sometimes a self-hosted local server such as LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp, sometimes an obscure OpenAI-compatible vendor not in Routers catalog. There is no operator key anywhere in this file. The url.includes check at line 214 and the default modelName literal at line 331 are internal details of this same construction, not separate call sites. Routing through a single shared RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY would merge unrelated end users billing and credentials into the operators Router account, which is not something a reasonable engineer would accept for a widely distributed BYOK extension, and there is no secure place in a public browser bundle to hold an operator secret anyway.
